previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: The patient was admitted with right-sided abdominal and flank pain described as a burning sensation, initially of unknown cause. Imaging ruled out acute abdominal pathology, diverticulitis, or obstruction. A vesicular rash developed along the right T5/6 dermatome, leading to a diagnosis of localized varicella zoster (shingles) by dermatology, despite a negative viral swab. She was treated with IV acyclovir, later transitioned to oral valacyclovir, with clinical improvement. Liver enzymes were elevated, attributed to possible hepatic zoster or GVHD, prompting an increase in prednisone from 15mg to 20mg daily and initiation of Bactrim for PCP prophylaxis. Epigastric pain emerged late in the admission, managed with Maalox and ranitidine after normal amylase, lipase, and imaging. The patient stabilized, pain improved with pregabalin, and she was discharged home on updated medications with follow-up planned.

radiology_notes.text:
HISTORY:  ___ female with AML.

STUDY:  Bilateral lower extremity venous ultrasound.

COMPARISON:  None.

FINDINGS:  Grayscale and color Doppler sonographic imaging performed of the
bilateral common femoral, superficial femoral, popliteal, peroneal, posterior
tibial veins.  In the left lower leg, duplicated posterior tibial veins are
demonstrated.  Both are non-compressibile with no discernible color flow, and
a subtle venous waveform, all compatible with non-occlusive thrombus.  The
remaining veins demonstrate normal compressibility, flow, and augmentation.

IMPRESSION:  Non-occlusive DVT of the left posterior tibial veins; this
finding was communicated to ___ at 17:04 on ___ by ___
___ over the phone.

INDICATION:  ___ woman with left lower extremity DVT, worsening
dyspnea.

COMPARISON:  ___.

TECHNIQUE:  MDCT data were acquired before and after the administration of
intravenous contrast.  Images were displayed in multiple planes including
oblique projections.

FINDINGS:  Contrast bolus timing is suboptimal for evaluation of the pulmonary
arteries as the images were acquired in an arterial phase.  Despite these
limitations, a filling defect is clearly noted at the junction of the right
middle and lower lobe pulmonary arteries (3:46, 402B:35).  Thrombus extends
down the right lower lobe pulmonary artery (3:48) and fills several right
basilar branches (3:52).  Thrombus also appears in the right upper lobe
pulmonary artery (3:35).  The left main and segmental pulmonary arteries are
patent.  Poor bolus timing limits detection of subsegmental emboli.  An
equivocal filling defect is seen in the anterior basal left pulmonary artery
(3:61).

No new nodules, consolidations, or effusions are seen in the lungs.  A 4-mm
right upper lobe granuloma is unchanged (2:21).  Calcified nodes are seen at
the left hilus (2:35).  The airways are patent to the subsegmental level.  No
pathologic mediastinal, hilar, or axillary adenopathy is present.  Coronary
artery calcifications are seen in the proximal LAD (2:25).  Thyroid gland
enhances homogeneously.  The visualized portions of the upper abdomen
demonstrate homogenously enhancing portions of the liver.  A tiny splenic
granuloma is noted.  The adrenal glands are normal.  Upper poles of both
kidneys enhance and excrete contrast symmetrically.  Surgical clips are seen
in the cholecystectomy bed and one clip is posterior to the right lobe of the
liver (3:10).  An 8-mm coarse calcification in the medial right breast is
unchanged since ___.

IMPRESSION:  Acute pulmonary emboli to the right upper, middle, and lower
pulmonary arteries.

Initial findings were reported by Dr. ___ at midnight, ___.
Final findings were discussed via telephone with Dr. ___ at 11:00 a.m. on
___.
